text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa on Thursday unveiled a Z$64 billion budget that was short on new ideas to revive economic growth but was laced with governmnet promises to continue implementing measures to restore macro-economic stability.

- Zimbabwe's central bank this week revised downwards this year's expected economic growth from five percent to 4.5 percent, saying the poor performance of the key agricultural sector had scuttled hopes of the country sustaining the high output of 8.1 percent recorded last year.
- The government intends to amend the Electoral Act so that all urban and rural district elections are conducted using the national voters roll instead of municipal rolls.

- Finance minister Herbert Murerwa on Thursday presented a no-shock budget which, as before, promised to bolster the country's economic recovery by reducing government's excessive spending and enhancing revenue collection.
- Air Zimbabwe has finally extricated itself from a controversial contract in which it leased two faulty Fokker 50 aircrafts from a Dtch company and lost millions of dollars.
